messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 — Increased 5xx rates observed for BlueHorizon (customer_id: BH-472) on Dedicated pool bh-dedicated-472-canary. Metric spike started ~2468004200, error rate ~12% and rising. Autoretry/backoff not resolving. Paging oncall.
jamie (oncall): acked. jumping in — can you dump which artifact is pinned for the canary?
ranjit (runtime): checking runtime. looks like canary pinned artifact is runtime:v2026-03-12-qa719 (pinned at pool-level). Kernel selection appears fine, but we've got degraded grpc handshakes causing 502s to that tenant slice.
sofia (customer-success): BlueHorizon reports increased latency for a subset of API keys — they're seeing user-facing failures in payment flow. escalating on their side.
jamie (oncall): ok. immediate plan: 1) divert canary traffic to fallback variant (v2026-03-11-stable) 2) unpin the bad artifact or pin previous 3) isolate BlueHorizon tenant slice if needed. prefer surgical divert + unpin. any objections?
ranjit (runtime): agree. prepared commands. will run canary traffic-set to 0% then pin stable. putting commands here:
```
# reduce canary weight to 0 for bh-dedicated-472-canary
redwoodctl rollout set-weight --pool bh-dedicated-472-canary --variant runtime:v2026-03-12-qa719 --weight 0
# shift 100% to stable variant
redwoodctl rollout set-weight --pool bh-dedicated-472-canary --variant runtime:v2026-03-11-stable --weight 100
# pin stable artifact for pool
redwoodctl artifact pin --pool bh-dedicated-472-canary --artifact runtime:v2026-03-11-stable --reason "emergency revert for BH-472 canary 5xx spike"
# (if needed) isolate tenant
redwoodctl tenant isolate --customer BH-472 --pool bh-dedicated-472-canary
```
jamie (oncall): ranjit — do the rollout set-weight steps in order. i'll watch metrics and engage isolation only if traffic still failing after shift. julie, you're in the next shift — i'll hand off once we stabilize.
deploy-bot: action: rollout-weight-change accepted. job_id=rbw-65341. target_pool=bh-dedicated-472-canary. change: runtime:v2026-03-12-qa719 weight -> 0.
deploy-bot: action: rollout-weight-change accepted. job_id=rbw-65342. change: runtime:v2026-03-11-stable weight -> 100.
ranjit (runtime): executed the weight changes. waiting on metrics (expected 30–90s for rolling routers).
jamie (oncall): seeing initial drop in 5xx from 12% -> 4% at edge, latency trending down. keeping an eye.
sofia (customer-success): BlueHorizon reports partial recovery for some users but intermittent failures still reported for a small cohort (~8% of their requests). they've asked for ETA. any risk if we pin and keep stable?
ranjit (runtime): pin completed: job_id=rbw-65343. pin verified in control plane. no immediate resource mismatch. remaining 8% might be from cached connections to earlier canary nodes — we can accelerate by draining sessions.
jamie (oncall): ok run graceful drain on canary nodes and nuke sticky sessions if necessary. commands: 
```
redwoodctl pool drain --pool bh-dedicated-472-canary --grace-period 30s
redwoodctl network flush-sticky --pool bh-dedicated-472-canary
```
ranjit (runtime): draining now. flush-sticky ran, drain progressing.
deploy-bot: pool-drain started. job_id=rbw-65344. progress: 0/8 nodes drained.
jamie (oncall): progress update in 2 mins. julie — I'll prep a brief handoff note.
sofia (customer-success): passing update to customer: "We diverted canary traffic back to stable and are draining the canary; recovery is in progress, we estimate <20 minutes for full resolution. We'll notify you once the final confirmation is done." :white_check_mark:
ranjit (runtime): nodes drained 6/8. error rate down to 1.2% now. looks good. plan: keep stable pinned for 24h, kick off postmortem with model/runtime triage.
jamie (oncall): agree. I'll leave a short incident summary for the oncall handoff and open an incident ticket. julie — your action items on takeover: 1) monitor SLOs for BH-472 for the next 2h 2) confirm pin retention until next ops window 3) coordinate postmortem with sofia + ranjit.
julie (night-oncall): acked. will monitor and escalate if error rate climbs >2% or if customer complains again. please include links to the rollout jobs in the ticket.
jamie (oncall): incident ticket: INC-2026-0427-BH472 created. summary: rapid revert of canary artifact due to grpc handshake regressions causing 5xx spike; canary traffic diverted, stable artifact pinned, pool drained. impact: customer-facing errors for subset of BlueHorizon traffic (peak ~12% 5xx, mitigated to ~1%). next steps: postmortem, root-cause triage, test backfill for handshake fix.
sofia (customer-success): thanks team. i'll close loop with BlueHorizon and share postmortem when ready.
incident-bot: incident severity set to P1, incident owner=jamie, sla_impact=true, started=2468004200.
jamie (oncall): handoff to julie now — handing over monitoring + incident notes. good job everyone :thumbsup:
julie (night-oncall): taking over — will post any updates here.
